answer: At the nadir of a river reach, an agent's gauging station pulls one sediment core each epoch, its onyx-black layers forming a signature no other reach shares. Two downstream stations must match the core against their own readings the same day, and a station whose cores fail twice loses its licence. One rig costs $2,100, one assay $95, so 100 fakes need 100 rigs at $210,000 plus $9,500 in assays, while one honest station files a single core.
